claim: The current benchmark controller completed strict end-to-end Goal Plus Search runs through both Codex and Pi, including bound parallel workers, worker feedback, continuation, deterministic controller closeout, promotion, and the common final evaluator.

protocol.credential_policy: OPENAI_API_KEY inherited from the shell and unset after the runs; no credential or endpoint is retained in this evidence

acceptance_gates: exactly one prepared Goal Plus record and one linked Search run
a bound native worker for every candidate and zero unbound sessions
no early exit before the no-target exploration minimum
Search run promoted and report persisted
selected artifact evaluated by the common final evaluator
setup and timed-plus-closeout evaluator calls reported separately

accepted_runs.usage_coverage: top-level Codex terminal usage unavailable; durable worker session counters and Search state retained in the ignored raw run

diagnostic_runs_rejected_by_new_gates.reason: The parent created two sessions per candidate but bound none before deadline. Controller closeout alone previously made this look finished; the strict validator now marks it incomplete.
Workers and continuations ran, but the no-target search exited after 176.659 seconds, below the 240-second exploration minimum. The strict validator now marks it incomplete.

fixes_validated: prepared-run prompt skips redundant large status calls
CandidateProposal uses the exact intent-only schema
one start_agent_session and one native launch per candidate
duplicate or unbound sessions fail the run
duplicate Goal Plus records linked to the prepared run fail the run
60-second worker dispatches allow same-lineage continuations within a five-minute cap
early no-target completion fails below the exploration minimum
controller closeout applies a non-empty promotion patch before final evaluation
interpretation: This validates the control flow on one easy task. It is not evidence that Goal Plus beats OpenEvolve or plain Codex; a benchmark campaign still needs multiple tasks, seeds, and symmetric usage telemetry.
